# ArrayObjectPool

**Class** · `ironwood.pool.ArrayObjectPool`

```java
public final class ArrayObjectPool<E extends Object> implements ObjectPool<E>
```

**Implements:** [`ObjectPool<E>`](ObjectPool.md)

Reuses objects in a resizable array with configurable preloading and growth.
Constructors can preload all or part of the initial capacity. A checkout
builds a value only when its next available slot is empty.



This single-threaded pool retains every builder-created object, including
checked-out objects. Return each checkout at most once, only to its originating
pool. Neither checkout nor return resets state or closes resources. Stop using
a returned object until a later checkout. These caller obligations have no
identity lookup or checkout-state bookkeeping on the reuse path.



Builder results must be fresh and unescaped. Reuse allocates no pool storage
after warmup. Creating a value records one reference; exhausted storage grows
by the configured factor, rounded down but by at least one slot. Superseded
arrays and a dropped pool graph become eligible for explicit collection.
External objects are outside the return contract.



This complete example exits 0 when a returned item is reused:


```java
import ironwood.pool.ArrayObjectPool;
import ironwood.pool.ObjectBuilder;
import ironwood.pool.ObjectPool;
class Item { int value; }
class ItemBuilder implements ObjectBuilder<Item> {
    @Override public Item newInstance() { return new Item(); }
}
public class PoolExample {
    public static int main(String[] args) {
        ItemBuilder builder = new ItemBuilder();
        ObjectPool<Item> pool = new ArrayObjectPool<Item>(4, 0, builder);
        Item first = pool.get();
        first.value = 42;
        pool.release(first);
        Item reused = pool.get();
        int result = reused.value == 42 ? 0 : 1;
        pool.release(reused);
        return result;
    }
}
```

### `ArrayObjectPool(int,int,ObjectBuilder<E>,float)`

```java
public ArrayObjectPool(int initialCapacity, int preloadCount, ObjectBuilder<E> builder, float growthFactor)
```

Creates a pool with explicit capacity, preload count, and growth factor.



Allocates both array containers and calls `builder.newInstance()`
exactly `preloadCount` times. Remaining slots are populated lazily.
The builder must be non-null and return a fresh unescaped value or null;
the compiler checks this contract. A null during preloading leaves an empty slot that is
retried on checkout; a null returned during checkout causes
`IllegalStateException`. Builder exceptions propagate to the caller.
The constructor does not explicitly validate the builder reference.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `initialCapacity` | the initial number of slots, greater than zero |
| `preloadCount` | the number of values built immediately, from zero through `initialCapacity`, inclusive |
| `builder` | the non-null factory retained for future checkouts |
| `growthFactor` | a finite multiplier greater than `1.0f` |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`IllegalArgumentException`](../lang/IllegalArgumentException.md) | if `initialCapacity < 1`, if the preload count is outside its range, or if the growth factor is non-finite or at most `1.0f` |

## Methods

<a name="member-get-28--29-"></a>

### `get()`

```java
@Override
public final E get()
```

Checks out the next available value, creating it if the slot is empty.



Grows the backing array when all current slots have been checked out.
A retained value is removed from its slot before being returned. The
caller can return it with [`release(E)`](#member-release-28-E-29-) after use. A reused value
keeps its previous state. Builder exceptions propagate to the caller.

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`IllegalStateException`](../lang/IllegalStateException.md) | if the builder returns null during checkout |

**Returns**

a non-null checked-out managed value

<a name="member-release-28-E-29-"></a>

### `release(E)`

```java
@Override
public final void release(E instance)
```

Returns a checked-out value for reuse without changing its state.



Return each checkout at most once, only to this pool. Stop using it
until it is checked out again. Duplicate returns are not checked.
External objects are unsupported.
When no return slot is available, the backing array grows while preserving
its available values. This method does not touch the creation array.

**Parameters**

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `instance` | the non-null checked-out value to make available |

**Throws**

| Exception | Condition |
| --- | --- |
| [`IllegalArgumentException`](../lang/IllegalArgumentException.md) | if `instance` is null |
